# odr-padenc

**Encodes the text and images that ride alongside a DAB service**

- **Version recorded:** 3.0.0
- **Categories:** `broadcast`, `sdr-toolkits`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/Opendigitalradio/ODR-PadEnc>
- **Not a recommended default** — installed only when asked for.

## What it does

Produces Programme Associated Data for a DAB service: the dynamic label that scrolls the track name across a receiver, and the slideshow images that accompany it, encoded and paced to fit the bit rate reserved for them.

## Why you would want it

PAD is what makes a DAB service look finished on a receiver. A station with no dynamic label and no slides is technically correct and visibly amateur, and this is the piece that fixes that.

## Before it will work

odr-audioenc to carry the encoded PAD alongside the audio, and a source for the text and images -- typically a playout system writing a file this watches.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install odr-padenc --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `odr-padenc`

## Known problems

PAD shares the service's bit rate, so generous slideshow settings cost audio quality; this trade is not automatic and is the usual thing to get wrong. Receivers vary in how much of the standard they implement and a slide that looks right in one may not appear in another.

- strategy: apt_upgrade
